proof_summary: Congruences give \(2^{58n+26}\equiv204\pmod{233}\), while \(2^{233}\equiv1\pmod{1399}\) and \(2^{206}\equiv-3\pmod{1399}\), proving divisibility by \(1399\). For every smaller prime, Fermat-style exponent reduction makes divisibility periodic in \(n\) and a finite modular computation excludes it, except that divisibility by \(67,271,523\) forces respectively \(n\equiv2\pmod5\), \(11\pmod{18}\), or \(26\pmod{42}\), each of which implies coverage by one of the three excluded cases.
